title: PalmPilot Personal Digital Assistant
summary: The groundbreaking handheld personal digital assistant that popularized mobile contact management, calendars, and Graffiti handwriting recognition.
facts: Introduced the Palm OS and Graffiti gesture-based text input system.
Shipped with 512KB to 1MB of RAM and ran on AAA batteries for weeks.
Synchronized seamlessly with desktop PCs via a HotSync cradle.

title: Iomega Zip Drive
summary: A super-floppy disk drive system offering 100MB of removable storage, revolutionizing data backup and file transfer before writable CDs became affordable.
facts: Replaced standard 1.44MB floppy disks for large files and backups.
Connected via parallel port, SCSI, or later USB.
Famous for the dreaded 'Click of Death' failure mode in some drive batches.

title: Sony Discman (G-Protection Series)
summary: Portable CD player featuring advanced G-Protection electronic anti-skip memory, allowing uninterrupted playback during movement.
facts: Solves the notorious playback skip issue of earlier portable CD players.
Used dual optical pickup buffering technology.
Helped CDs dominate portable music listenership in the late 90s.

title: DVD Format & Commercial Launch
summary: Digital Versatile Disc optical media format offering pristine MPEG-2 digital video, 5.1 surround audio, and interactive menus, superseding VHS.
facts: First commercially launched in Japan in November 1996 and North America in early 1997.
Offered 4.7 GB capacity on single-layer discs compared to 700 MB on CDs.
Featured regional encoding and Dolby Digital AC-3 audio tracks.

title: Apple iMac G3
summary: Translucent Bondi Blue all-in-one desktop computer designed by Jony Ive that revitalized Apple and eliminated legacy floppy drives in favor of USB and Ethernet.
facts: First consumer Mac featuring USB ports as standard equipment.
Ditched the 3.5-inch floppy drive, accelerating the move toward web downloads and CDs.
Powered by PowerPC 750 (G3) processor at 233 MHz.
